studies.label: Story writing with and without ChatGPT, randomized condition order

counts_source.quote: In total, our final sample consisted of 263 participants

arms.name: AI-help
arms.description: Story written with free access to a ChatGPT side textbox. A hidden system prompt limited output to bullet-point ideas and prevented entire story passages; copy-paste was disabled (PDF p. 10, Story Writing Task; Appendix A, PDF p. 32). Each analyzed participant completed this condition.

arms.name: No-AI
arms.description: Story written in the matched interface with the ChatGPT textbox removed (PDF p. 10, Story Writing Task; Appendix B, PDF p. 32). Participants were instructed to use the suggested prompting strategies as self-directed brainstorming (PDF p. 11). Each analyzed participant completed this condition.

studies.task: Introductory psychology students at Pennsylvania State University wrote a creative short story using all words of an assigned prompt, once with ChatGPT and once without it; prompts were counterbalanced across conditions (PDF pp. 8-10).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT based on the GPT 3.5 base model, accessed through a custom API
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 10, Method, Story Writing Task

preregistration.where: Not stated in the paper; PDF p. 8 names originality and diversity as the main outcomes.

studies.shared_sample: Study 1 of c475, Luchini, Kaufman, and Beaty, Generative AI Does Not Erase Individual Differences in Human Creativity, reanalyzes this sample according to forms/c159.json, sample_overlap. This relationship is carried from the reconciled form as instructed; the c159 PDF does not name the later paper.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Multilingual Assessment of Short Stories (MAoSS), a fine-tuned LLM on the Creativity Assessment Platform trained to predict human-rated story originality (PDF p. 11, Scoring, Originality). The original score scale is 0-1 (PDF p. 18, Self-Assessment Accuracy: "Because MAoSS scores were on a different scale (0 – 1)").

paper_effect.standardizer: Not stated for the reported d from the paired-samples t-test.

estimates.notes: Full-sample paired-samples t-test; each participant contributed a story in both conditions. Both arm SDs are literally printed as "SD = 08" in the PDF text and in the rendered page. Their intended decimal placement cannot be confirmed, so treatment_sd, control_sd, and sd_level are null; no corrected SD was inferred. The printed confidence interval is retained, but its target is not explicitly identified: ci_of is null, and the interval is not assigned to paper_effect. No raw difference, SE, SD of paired differences, or within-person correlation is printed. The paper identifies originality and diversity as its main outcomes (PDF p. 8), but does not state preregistration. Figure 2 (PDF p. 15) supplies graphical intervals, not additional printed arm bounds; no values were read off the figure. No first-round-only contrast is reported.

estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Leave-one-out contribution of a story to the mean pairwise semantic distance of all stories for its prompt. Final-layer sentence embeddings come from paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2; prompt words are removed before embedding (PDF pp. 11-12, Scoring, Diversity Contribution). Semantic distance is one minus cosine similarity. Contribution equals the complete prompt-pool mean pairwise distance minus the mean after removing that story. Positive contributions indicate that the story adds diversity. The analysis compares participant-level contributions, with one story per participant per condition.

paper_effect.standardizer: Not stated for the reported d from the paired-samples t-test.

estimates.notes: Full-sample paired-samples t-test across participants, so se_basis records the paper's participant-level uncertainty. Each condition supplies one story per participant; n_total counts each participant once. The underlying semantic distances use all pairs in a prompt-defined pool, but pairs are not the independent observations in the reported t-test. Pools are split by prompt rather than condition (PDF pp. 11-12); because prompts are counterbalanced across conditions (PDF p. 9), these pools mix AI-help and No-AI stories. The recorded arm levels are means of per-story diversity contributions to those mixed pools, not within-arm set-level diversity. The paper's paired test does not describe an adjustment for dependence induced by the shared pools. Values retain the raw units printed in the Results; Figure 2 uses a display multiplier that is not applied here (PDF p. 15). The printed confidence interval is retained with ci_of null because the target is not explicitly identified, and is not assigned to paper_effect. No raw difference, SE, SD of paired differences, or within-person correlation is printed. The negative contrast indicates less diversity with AI. No first-round-only contrast is reported.

open_items: Originality arm SDs are printed as "08" without a decimal point (PDF p. 14). Their intended values are unconfirmed and the numeric SD fields remain null.
The targets of the printed confidence intervals and the standardizers of the reported d values are not stated (PDF pp. 14 and 17); ci_of remains null and no standardizer is inferred.
Neither eligible contrast prints an SE, SD of within-person differences, or within-person correlation. No such quantity is derived for this transcription.

No first-round-only estimates or order/carryover analyses are printed. Everyone completed a practice story with ChatGPT available before both scored conditions, but actual practice use is not established (PDF pp. 9-11).
The count at random assignment, counts by condition order, and exclusions by condition order are not printed; a recruited sample count is not substituted for n_randomized (PDF pp. 8-9).
Within-arm set-level diversity is not printed. The diversity outcome measures story contributions to prompt pools that mix conditions (PDF pp. 9 and 11-12).
The paper names the ChatGPT/GPT 3.5 model but does not state its release year or exact API snapshot (PDF p. 10); ai_tool.year is null.
notes: Extracted on 2026-10-09 by extractor A; not independently reviewed in this file. The complete markdown conversion, including references and appendices, was read in order. Every cited PDF page was checked with pymupdf; the malformed originality SDs and Appendix A/B screenshots were also inspected as PDF renders. The PDF has no printed page numbers; all locators use file page order. All analyzed participants completed both conditions in randomized order (PDF p. 9), so the same people appear in both arms and counts are not added across conditions. No distinct after_ai comparison is reported. Prior AI availability in the practice task and possible carryover into No-AI are limitations of the paired comparison. No statistics were computed from the posted data, from effect-size formulas, or from figures. Sources preserve the printed decimal forms even where JSON serializes small numbers in scientific notation.
